answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through bonded identity plus peer attestation. Every agent posts a stake before joining the grove of active workers, so mass-producing pseudonyms becomes costly instead of free. New identities start on a shale layer of reduced trust, earning full weight only as established peers thread verified work through their signatures over time. A caught attacker loses that stake and every attestation it threaded, collapsing the whole fake clique in one stroke, making one honest agent far cheaper to keep than a thousand fakes.
